questions.q: What does encryption at rest protect against, and what MongoDB feature implements it?
options: Someone reading raw data from stolen disks or unencrypted backups; implemented via the Encrypted Storage Engine (WiredTiger, AES-256)
Network eavesdropping on queries in transit; implemented via TLS
SQL injection attacks against the database
Unauthorized users creating new collections
questions.explain: Encryption at rest protects data files on disk, implemented in MongoDB via the Encrypted Storage Engine.

questions.q: Is encryption at rest available in MongoDB Community Server?
options: No — it's genuinely an Enterprise/Atlas feature, not available in Community
Yes, it's available and enabled by default in Community
Yes, but only for the admin database
It was available in Community but was removed in recent versions
questions.explain: The Encrypted Storage Engine requires MongoDB Enterprise or Atlas — this is a real licensing distinction from encryption in transit.

options: Rejects any connection that doesn't use TLS at all — the recommended production setting
Encrypts data files on disk automatically
Disables authentication in favor of certificate-only access
Allows both encrypted and unencrypted connections equally
questions.explain: requireTLS is the strict mode that rejects non-TLS connections entirely, as opposed to weaker modes that merely allow TLS.

questions.q: Is encryption in transit (TLS/SSL) available in MongoDB Community Server?
options: Yes — unlike encryption at rest, TLS is available in Community Server with no Enterprise license required
No, TLS requires MongoDB Enterprise or Atlas
TLS is only available for connections within the same data center
TLS was deprecated in favor of a proprietary MongoDB protocol
questions.explain: TLS/SSL for encryption in transit is available in Community Server, the key licensing contrast with at-rest encryption.

questions.q: On MongoDB Atlas, how is encryption at rest typically handled?
options: Automatically, as part of the managed service — you don't configure the storage engine yourself
It must be manually enabled via mongod.conf on each Atlas node
Atlas does not support encryption at rest at all
It requires purchasing a separate Enterprise license on top of Atlas
questions.explain: Atlas, as a managed service, handles at-rest encryption automatically without manual storage-engine configuration.
